Customer wants low-lift proof-of-concept, cares about latency/cost tradeoffs, SSO/KMS, and private deployment options for regulated data. Agreed to quickstart run and SE deep dive to follow.
transcript:
Date: 2026-09-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SDR); Lena Ortiz (Novus Edge CTO), Marco Diaz (Sr ML Engineer), Priya Singh (Head of Platform), Oscar Kim (DevOps)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Avery from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick agenda — run a short discovery, cover our PLG quickstart flow (free credits, time-to-first-token), and then see if there are any blockers for a short POC, cool?
[00:18] Lena: Yeah thanks, yeah that works. we have about 45 minutes. quick background — Novus Edge is building a customer support summarization and search layer, heavy embedding use plus some generation for templates and macros. we evaluate hosted initially but definitely looking at dedicated or private once we go into prod.
[00:35] Samir: great, can you share current stack? what are you using for embeddings and hosting?
[00:42] Marco: right now we're using a mix — embeddings on OpenAI for the prototype, some local models for offline tasks. infra is AWS, we use EKS, and some strict network controls, we might need VPC egress rules for a private deploy.
[01:05] Avery: perfect, that tells us a lot. our quickstart is intentionally low friction — sign up, get a free credits bundle, we have a sample repo and a Postman/curl quickstart that gets you to first token in under 10 minutes in most cases.
[01:20] Priya: can you explain the difference between hosted, dedicated and private again? we want to understand operational and security tradeoffs.
[01:28] Samir: sure — hosted is our managed API, fastest to try, pay-as-you-go, we give credits to evaluate. Dedicated is reserved capacity (you get a GPU pool and isolation) — predictable latency and throughput. Private is for VPC or on-prem where the control plane is customer-managed, so you can keep data inside your network and integrate KMS/HSM.
[01:55] Oscar: for private, how does SSO and audit logs work? we need SOC2-like audit trails and SSO for team access.
[02:03] Samir: we integrate with SAML/SSO, RBAC is available, and audit logs can be configured to forward to your SIEM. we also support KMS for key wrapping and customer-managed keys in private deployments. note: some of the terms in our docs get parsed as Red wood — sometimes the transcript autocorrects, but it's Redwood.
[02:26] Lena: ok great. what's the usual timeline from sign-up to a test workload?
[02:33] Avery: for most teams, time-to-first-token is minutes — like sign up, link a billing or use credits, paste your prompt and go. for a meaningful eval (embeddings + generation + a small traffic test), plan 1-2 weeks to run and capture latency/cost metrics.
[02:50] Marco: do you give a sandbox with sample embeddings index?
[02:55] Samir: yes we have sample datasets and an eval harness. we'll also send a benchmark sheet where you can plug in your prompt set and we run tests across sequence lengths.
[03:10] Jordan: quick Q — do you have prebuilt SDKs for Python, JS?
[03:14] Avery: yes python and node, plus REST. we also have examples for common frameworks like LangChain.
[03:22] Marco: cost — how does token billing compare? we're worried about costs with high-query embedding workloads.
[03:30] Samir: embeddings are billed per embedding unit; we recommend batching and caching prefixes. Redwood Optimize suggests batching settings and quantization profiles to lower unit costs. Also you can route heavy workloads to dedicated pools or to a cheaper quantized model for non-sensitive work.
[03:54] Priya: any limits on the free credits or expirations?
[03:58] Avery: credits usually expire in 30 days, amount depends on promo but it's sufficient to run a small POC. we can also extend them if the POC looks promising while you run the SE-led bench.
[04:12] Lena: in terms of security, we have to pass legal and security review — do you publish SOC2 or ISO certs?
[04:20] Samir: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs for hosted. for private deployments we provide the architecture docs, and we can share a security pack for legal.
[04:34] Marco: technical question — how does KV cache and batching work? we need consistent latency for chat flows.
[04:41] Samir: runtime does continuous batching, KV cache management — caching prefixes and reusing KV states for short-turnaround chat. that lowers cost and keeps latency stable. for very latency-sensitive flows, dedicated pools with smaller batching windows are recommended.
[05:05] Oscar: network — if we want VPC peering or a private endpoint, is that supported in the quickstart?
[05:12] Avery: quickstart is hosted, we can demo VPC/private options later in a dedicated or private deployment conversation. quickstart gets you started on hosted.
[05:22] Lena: are there any gotchas with the sign-up flow behind enterprise SSO? sometimes our users can't use email sign-up.
[05:29] Avery: for SSO-only teams we can create an enterprise invite and seed the account; or you can create a service account for the initial test and then we'll map identities later. we'll put instructions in the guide.
[05:45] Marco: curious about latencies — what are typical P95s for generation and embedding?
[05:50] Samir: depends on model and sequence length; for our curated open models on hosted, generation p95 for short prompts is ~200-600ms, embeddings typically <100ms for small models. dedicated can bring that down and reduce variance. these are rough numbers — we'll run your prompts in the bench to provide numbers.
[06:12] Priya: what's the rollback story if a model update causes regressions?
[06:18] Samir: we support rollouts and pinned model versions — you can pin a version per route and use canary or A/B. Redwood Console has eval hooks to detect regressions against your prompt sets.
[06:33] Lena: in terms of compliance, do you store payloads? we need controllable retention.
[06:39] Samir: retention is configurable; hosted retains logs for X days by default but we can offer stricter retention or no storage in private deployments. we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[06:55] Jordan: can we do a small load test from our side? like 50 QPS embeddings for a few minutes to see burst behavior?
[07:02] Samir: yes we'll coordinate rate limits and we'll provide a small bench token so you don't hit rate limits. if you want sustained load we'll talk about a short-term dedicated burst.
[07:18] Marco: are there any known integration issues with EKS or internal NAT policies?
[07:24] Samir: generally fine; for private deployments we need network diagrams and firewall rules. for hosted we use standard HTTPS endpoints, so NAT is usually okay but egress rules must allow outbound to Redwood API endpoints.
[07:42] Lena: do you support customer-managed KMS in hosted or only private?
[07:47] Samir: customer-managed KMS is primarily in private deployments; we can do some key wrapping options for hosted but full HSM integration is private. we'll note that clearly.
[07:59] Avery: quick note on pricing — hosted is usage-based; dedicated is contractual reserved capacity; private is licensing + support. we'll send a pricing link but it's negotiable depending on committed usage.
[08:18] Priya: how heavy is the setup for a dedicated pool?
[08:22] Samir: dedicated pools need capacity planning, but we can do a short-term reserved trial for 30 days to validate throughput. for long-term you pick a monthly/annual commit.
[08:35] Marco: any tips to reduce token spend in generation?
[08:39] Samir: prompt engineering (shorter contexts), prefix caching, streaming to avoid re-sends, and using smaller models for parts of the pipeline. Optimize has suggestions per workload.
[08:55] Lena: let's talk about quickstart steps — can you walk us through the exact five things to do?
[09:01] Avery: sure — 1) sign up and claim free credits, 2) run the quickstart sample (python example) to get a token and make a text-gen call, 3) run the embeddings example and index a small dataset, 4) run the eval harness (we'll provide the sheet) to test latency/cost, 5) sync with SE to review results and plan next steps.
[09:26] Marco: that seems doable. any docs for the eval harness?
[09:30] Samir: yes we'll attach the bench spreadsheet and a runbook.
[09:35] Oscar: we have regulatory concerns in EU, data residency — can hosted route to eu regions?
[09:40] Avery: yes we have EU regions for hosted; private deployments are available if you need strict residency or on-prem controls.
[09:48] Lena: ok, what would you need from us to get started?
[09:51] Avery: ideally sample prompt set, a small representative dataset for embeddings, and a contact for the SE deep dive. once we have that we can seed the quickstart and issue credits.
[10:05] Priya: timeline — we want to present to legal next week, can we get security docs before then?
[10:10] Samir: yes we'll share the security pack (SOC2, ISO, network diagrams, retention options) by tomorrow.
[10:18] Jordan: i'll drop the quickstart links and instructions in the meeting notes too.
[10:24] Lena: perfect. anything else?
[10:27] Avery: quick clarifier — for time-to-first-token, is CI/CD or automation important? you mentioned some server-side jobs.
[10:34] Marco: we want to automate embedding updates and have a lambda that calls the API, so service account tokens and kms integration matter.
[10:41] Samir: service accounts and scoped API keys are supported; we'll include best practices for secret rotation.
[10:49] (crosstalk) Speaker 1: ummm
[10:53] Priya: can you confirm the free credit expiry again?
[10:56] Avery: 30 days usually, we'll confirm amount in the follow-up email.
[11:02] Lena: ok great, let's kick off.

[34:10] (note: meeting continued with detailed technical discussion; timestamps jump forward to capture key follow ups)
[34:10] Samir: on the bench run, we'll need sequence lengths, sample prompts, and target QPS. we'll provide a template.
[34:24] Marco: i'll prepare prompt sets and expected distribution.
[34:30] Priya: SE deep dive — can we include a session focused on private deployment checklist? network, KMS, and audit logs specifically.
[34:38] Samir: yes we can do a private-deploy checklist session.
[34:44] Avery: recap of next steps — i'll send quickstart guide + free credits, Samir will schedule SE deep dive and bench, Lena will share prompt set and traffic profile.
[34:55] Lena: fine. thanks everyone.
[35:00] Avery: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links and the security pack.

[46:30] (call end)

References/links mentioned: Quickstart repo link (shared in follow-up), Security pack (SOC2/ISO), Bench spreadsheet (send), Pricing page (send link).
